extraFacts.fact: Wave 4 products are API certified and supplied with the API monogram by API-licensed manufacturers to the applicable specification: API 6A, API 16A, API 16C, API 16D or API 7K.
NACE MR0175 / ISO 15156 sets material requirements for equipment used in H2S-containing oil and gas production.

API 6A product specification level (PSL 1 to 4) sets the inspection, testing and traceability applied; PR1 and PR2 are the performance requirement levels, PR2 having passed API 6A design-validation testing. PSL 3G adds a gas test.

faqs.q: What is a dual-pot vertical 10,000 psi sand filter used for?
faqs.a: A dual-pot sand filter removes sand and fines from well-test flow before it reaches chokes and downstream equipment. This vertical dual-pot unit is rated 10,000 psi MAWP, ASME U2-stamped, with an SS316 sintered cartridge filter element.

faqs.q: What do ASME U2 and SS316 sintered mean on this sand filter?
faqs.a: ASME U2 is the code stamp on the pressure vessel, and SS316 sintered describes the stainless steel sintered cartridge element that retains fines. The vessel is rated 10,000 psi MAWP.

faqs.q: What pressure ratings does the dual-pot sand filter come in?
faqs.a: The filter is available in 5K, 10K and 15K psi variants. This listing is the 10,000 psi unit in a vertical dual-pot arrangement on a DNV frame.

faqs.q: Can the dual-pot sand filter run one pot or both pots?
faqs.a: Yes. The inlet and outlet by-pass manifold allows single-pot or parallel operation, so one pot can be cleaned while the other stays on line.

faqs.q: How does the sand filter show that the cartridge is clogging?
faqs.a: Differential-pressure measurement between inlet and outlet drives a clogging alarm. Clean the cartridge by HP water-nozzle backwash when the alarm trips.

faqs.q: What is the sand filter element made from?
faqs.a: The element is an SS316 sintered cartridge, which retains fines after the internal shields drop the stream velocity and let heavy particles settle in the drain area.

faqs.q: Which codes apply to the 10,000 psi sand filter?
faqs.a: The listing states ASME U2 stamping and a DNV frame for offshore deployment. State any further certification, such as third-party witness, on the RFQ.

faqs.q: What does the dual-pot sand filter connect to?
faqs.a: It connects in the well-test flowline downstream of the choke manifold, through its inlet and outlet by-pass manifold. See the [desanders and debris catchers](/c/wt-desanders-debris-catchers) shelf for related sand handling and the [well testing equipment guide](/blog/surface-well-testing-equipment).

faqs.q: How is the cartridge changed on the dual-pot sand filter?
faqs.a: A deployable gantry crane lifts the cartridge out for removal or replacement without interrupting operations. Isolate and depressurise the pot first.

faqs.q: Sand filter or desander for well-test flowback?
faqs.a: A sand filter retains fines on a sintered cartridge, while a desander removes bulk sand upstream with cyclones or screened barrels. See the [desanders and debris catchers](/c/wt-desanders-debris-catchers) shelf for the other options.
